top_choice_rationale: P002 (Autor, Dorn, Hanson), with the citation confined to the import-competition and local-labour-market evidence. The three names jointly wrote the central China-shock papers, so the credit boundary is clean and the task-based lineage (Katz, Levy-Murnane, Acemoglu) is not claimed. The design answers a first-order question, who bears the costs of trade integration, with transparent quasi-experimental evidence. It has been replicated across countries. About a decade of scrutiny has refined magnitudes and exposed shift-share inference problems without overturning the finding that adjustment is slow, costly and geographically concentrated. I concede that P001 (Kiyotaki and Moore) has cleaner attribution and nearly three decades of use, and that P002 has a shorter record and contested effect sizes. The collateral-feedback mechanism is also distinct from the bank-run work recognised in 2022. I still weigh direct, credible identification of a first-order question above a mechanism whose quantitative validation is indirect, so P001 is a close second. P003 (Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn) is a mature and influential demand-estimation advance, but it depends more on functional-form and instrument assumptions and excludes the wider structural-IO strand. No award is ranked last because at least three proposals describe mature, well-attributed achievements.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile. The profile lists no co-authorship or institutional tie to Autor, Dorn, Hanson, Kiyotaki, Moore, Pakes, Berry or Levinsohn. His listed co-authors (Holmlund, Edin, Åslund, Öckert, Johansson, Nybom, Oosterbeek, van Ours) are not credited on any proposal. Disclosed field proximity: his research is in empirical labour economics and design-based evaluation, close to P002, and his 2021 presentation speech praised natural-experiment methods. These may bias him toward direct identification. They are disclosed, not adjudicated.
